Research algebraic methods for establishing a Jónsson-Tarski-style representation theorem for the bimodal logic TM with primitives Since (S), Until (U), and Box (□), plus material implication (→) and bottom (⊥) as the primitive Boolean operators. The goal is to determine whether the Lindenbaum-Tarski algebra of TM forms a variety of Boolean algebras with operators (BAOs) that admits a concrete representation into complex algebras of relational structures (task frames). Key questions: (1) Since S and U are binary normal operators, does the standard Jónsson-Tarski representation for n-ary BAOs apply directly, or does the interaction with the S5 modal operator □ introduce complications? (2) What role does orthodox axiomatizability (no IRR rule) play — per Venema 1993 (Anti-Axioms), orthodox systems ensure closure under ultraproducts, but TM uses the IRR rule in the ConservativeExtension module; does this affect the algebraic representation? (3) Can the existing TenseS5Algebra.lean structure be extended to a full BAO with S/U operators, and does the Lindenbaum quotient construction yield a representable algebra? (4) What is the relationship between the parametric representation theorem (ParametricRepresentation.lean) and a Jónsson-Tarski-style algebraic representation — are they equivalent, or does one subsume the other? (5) How do the Prior-UZ/SZ axioms (discrete well-ordering) and the uniformity axioms (ordered abelian group structure) interact with the algebraic representation? Literature base: Venema 1991 (dissertation Ch2 + App A), Venema 1993 (Anti-Axioms), Goldblatt-Hodkinson-Venema 2003, Venema 1997 (Atom Structures), de Rijke-Venema 1995 (Sahlqvist for BAOs), Blackburn-de Rijke-Venema 2001 Ch5 (not yet obtained). All papers are in literature/ with markdown conversions.

active_projects.description: Add time addition operator (+) to the bimodal logic TM. φ + ψ is true at (τ, x) iff ∃ y,z with x = y+z, φ true at (τ,y), ψ true at (τ,z). This internalizes the AddCommGroup structure of D into the object language, extending expressive power from FO[<] to FO[<,+] (Presburger arithmetic). Related to arrow logic (Venema), relevant logic (Routley-Meyer ternary frames), and separation logic (BI). Phase 1: add tadd/tsub constructors to Formula, truth clause in semantics. Phase 2: basic axioms (associativity, commutativity, identity, inverse). Phase 3: soundness proofs. Phase 4: interaction with G/H/U/S/□. Add topological open set (interior) operator for dense and continuous temporal frames. On discrete ℤ the interior is trivial (discrete topology), but on dense ℚ and continuous ℝ it captures neighborhood-stable truth: Int(φ) true at t iff φ holds in an open neighborhood of t. Related to Dynamic Topological Logic (Kremer-Mints 2005), McKinsey-Tarski topological semantics for S4, and Fernandez-Duque intuitionistic temporal logic. Phase 1: add TopologicalSpace instance to TaskFrame for dense/continuous cases. Phase 2: add interior constructor to Formula with truth clause. Phase 3: axioms (S4-like: Int(φ)→φ, Int(φ)→Int(Int(φ))). Phase 4: interaction with temporal operators and S5 □. Note: DTL is not finitely axiomatizable (Fernandez-Duque 2014) — completeness may require non-standard techniques.

active_projects.description:
Prove Doets 1989 Lemma 1.1 (finitely many formulas up to logical equivalence) and redesign KType with a finite normal form domain, closing ktype_finite and KEquivalenceFramework.finite_types.

The current KType definition uses an infinite domain ({s : MonadicFormula sig 0 // s.quantifier_depth <= k} -> Bool) which makes Fintype impossible. The correct mathematical object (Doets 1987 Chapter 1, Section 1.6-1.7) is the space of n-characteristics: for each quantifier depth k and variable count n, there are finitely many semantically distinct formulas.

Scope:

1. Define nfCount (p : Nat) (k : Nat) (n : Nat) : Nat — the number of semantically distinct monadic FO formulas of quantifier depth <= k with n free variables over a signature with p unary predicates and binary <. Following Doets 1987 Definition 1.6.1:
   - Depth 0, n vars: 2^(p*n + n*(n-1)/2) atomic types (one per truth assignment to atoms P_i(x_j) and x_i < x_j for i < j)
   - Depth k+1, n vars: 2^(nfCount p k (n+1)) (one per Boolean combination of depth-k formulas with one additional quantified variable)

2. Define NormalForm (sig : MonadicSignature) (k : Nat) (n : Nat) — a finite type of normal form representatives (Doets n-characteristics / Hintikka formulas). This can be Fin (nfCount sig.preds.card k n) or a custom inductive. Each normal form at depth 0 is a conjunction of literals over the atomic formulas P_i(x_j) and x_i < x_j. Each normal form at depth k+1 specifies, for each depth-k normal form with one extra variable, whether exists-x and forall-x versions hold.

3. Define nf_eval : NormalForm sig k n -> OrderedMonadicStructure sig -> (Fin n -> carrier) -> Prop — the semantic interpretation of each normal form. By structural recursion on the normal form.

4. Prove Doets Lemma 1.1 (the main theorem): for every MonadicFormula sig n with quantifier_depth <= k, there exists a NormalForm sig k n that is semantically equivalent (same truth value in every structure under every assignment). Proof by induction on k:
   - Base case (k=0): every quantifier-free formula is a Boolean combination of atoms; reduce to DNF over the finitely many atomic types.
   - Inductive step (k+1): a depth-(k+1) formula has the form Qx.phi where Q is forall/exists and phi has depth <= k with n+1 variables. By IH, phi is equivalent to a normal form in NormalForm sig k (n+1). The quantifier Qx applied to this normal form yields one of the depth-(k+1) normal forms.

5. Redefine KType sig k := NormalForm sig k 0 -> Bool (or equivalently Fin (nfCount sig.preds.card k 0) -> Bool). This is a function from a finite type to Bool, so Fintype (KType sig k) holds by inferInstance.

6. Redefine k_type_of to use the normal form factorization: k_type_of M maps each normal form to whether M satisfies it (via nf_eval).

7. Close ktype_finite: now Fintype (KType sig k) = inferInstance.

8. Close KEquivalenceFramework.finite_types: use Setoid.quotientKerEquivRange + Set.finite_range + Fintype.ofFinite.

9. Delete the old ktype_finite definition (dead code, mathematically impossible as stated).

10. Verify all downstream files compile (IntegerModel, OrderedSum, Transfer).

Definition of done: ktype_finite is sorry-free (or deleted and replaced by inferInstance), KEquivalenceFramework.finite_types is sorry-free, Doets Lemma 1.1 is stated and proved, lake build passes.

Literature: Doets 1987 Completeness and Definability thesis (Chapter 1, Sections 1.6-1.7: n-characteristics, Lemma 1.7.1), Doets 1989 Monadic Pi11 Theories (Lemma 1.1).

active_projects.description: Prove sum_preservation (NEquivalence.lean:190) and doets_lemma_1_4 (OrderedSum.lean:45): k-equivalence is preserved under ordered sums of monadic structures. This is the sole remaining sorry in the KEquivalenceFramework instance and blocks activation of the Reynolds pipeline. The proof follows Doets 1987 Lemma 1.4 using Ehrenfeucht-Fraisse games: given a k-round EF game on Sigma_I m(i) vs Sigma_I m'(i), the duplicator's winning strategy combines winning strategies on individual components. When the spoiler plays in component i, the duplicator responds using the i-th component strategy (from h_equiv i). When the spoiler switches components, the duplicator uses the order-preservation of the index set I. Also close the carrier_order sorries in the Sigma-type ordered sum construction (lexicographic order on Sigma). Once proved, chronicle_is_good and finite_structures_good become closable, unblocking task 155. Note: also requires closing contemp_equiv_is_equiv transitivity (IntegerModel.lean:128) and no_gaps_discrete (IntegerModel.lean:145) which depend on sum_preservation through very_good/good.
